Tuesday. Nitin had done everything on the checklist: the screenshots were saved, the complaint was in, the accounts were blocked. It felt like enough.
Saturday. Nitin was still sleeping badly and had a knot in the stomach on the way to school. Something was not fading. That evening Nitin thought, the checklist covers what to do, not how I am.
Monday. Nitin went to the school counsellor. The counsellor said, “I'm glad you came. What you feel makes sense.” They agreed to meet each week, and the counsellor offered to be with Nitin when telling the parents that afternoon.
Thursday. Nitin's cousin Gargi came over and they walked to the park, as they now do every Thursday, and just talked.

qa.q: Who did Nitin add to the plan besides the counsellor?
What did Nitin feel when noticing that the stress was not fading after the practical steps?
qa.a: Worry and unease: Nitin was still sleeping badly and felt a knot in the stomach on the way to school.

qa.q: What could Nitin do if things still feel heavy after some weeks, and why?
qa.a: Tell the counsellor and parents again, since more support may be needed and it is fine to ask.

qa.q: How does Nitin's reaching out look to Gargi?
qa.a: Gargi feels trusted by being chosen to talk with, and the weekly walks give Gargi a clear way to help.

grounding: A teen still sleeping badly notices the stress is not fading, tells the school counsellor and adds talks with a trusted cousin.

Madhav, you've done every practical thing right: screenshots, reports, telling your parents. I'm proud of you. But let me tell you what I missed when this happened to me.
I was sixteen. A group had been mocking me on a chat app, and I handled it like a project. Evidence, done. Blocked, done. School told, done. I thought that was all.
A week later I still couldn't sleep. I'd lie awake at two, replaying every comment. My marks slipped. One morning I fell asleep on the bus and missed my stop, and I thought: the problem is handled, but I'm not.
So I went to Mrs Kaur, the school counsellor, and told her about the nights, not the messages. She said, “Vasudha, the stress needs looking after too.” After that, every Sunday I called my cousin Nimmi, who just listened.
So, Madhav. Let's add a person to your plan, not only steps.

qa.q: Who did young Vasudha call every Sunday?
qa.a: A cousin, Nimmi, who just listened.

qa.q: What did young Vasudha feel lying awake at two in the morning?
qa.a: Vasudha felt anxious and worn out, replaying every comment even though the practical steps were done.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed Vasudha's plan?
qa.a: Falling asleep on the bus and missing the stop, which showed the problem was handled but Vasudha was not, and led to the counsellor.

qa.q: How might Mrs Kaur have seen Vasudha's visit?
qa.a: Mrs Kaur probably saw a student who had managed the facts well but needed care for the stress, and said so plainly.

grounding: An elder recalls still sleeping badly days after handling the practical steps, then telling the school counsellor and adding weekly talks with a cousin.

With pre-boards eleven days away, Jagdish had no time for feelings, or so he told himself. The fake account mocking him had been reported, the screenshots were with the school, and his parents had filed the complaint. Done.
Except he was still awake at three most nights, heart racing for no reason he could name. On Thursday he read the same page of chemistry four times and remembered none of it.
That was the signal. The logistics are sorted, he thought, but I'm not. He went to the school counsellor at lunch. She listened, then asked who he could talk to regularly, not about the account, just about how he was.
He thought of Eshaan, his cousin in Pune, who always made him laugh. That night he called. They agreed: every evening, ten minutes, after dinner. The first call ran for forty.
Two days later, Jagdish slept through to six.

qa.q: How many days away were the pre-boards?
What was Jagdish feeling when he couldn't remember the chemistry page?
qa.a: He was likely frightened and drained, seeing that the stress hadn't faded even though the practical steps were done.

qa.q: What else could Jagdish add if sleep stays poor?
qa.a: Tell his parents and go back to the counsellor, who can suggest further support if the stress keeps going.

qa.q: What might the calls mean for Eshaan?
qa.a: Eshaan gets to help in a simple way, just by talking, and likely feels trusted to be chosen.

grounding: Shows a teen who notices the stress is not fading days after handling the logistics, tells the school counsellor and adds regular talks with a cousin.
